designationHistory.name: Pikes Peak Timber Land Reserve
designationHistory.indexText: Pikes Peak Timber Land Reserve: Established reserve.

sources.name: Establishment and Modification of National Forest Boundaries: A Chronologic Record, 1891–1985 (USDA Forest Service, Lands Staff, 1985), PDF page 7
27 Stat. 1006 (Statutes at Large, govinfo): Proclamation No. 15, Feb. 11, 1892, Benjamin Harrison, forest reservation in Colorado
American Presidency Project: Proclamation 554, May 12, 1905, combining the Pikes Peak Timber Land Reserve and others as the Pikes Peak Forest Reserve

Davis, The National Forests of the United States (Encyclopedia of American Forest and Conservation History, App. I, 1983), Forest History Society PDF; compiled partly from an earlier edition of the Forest Service chronologic record, so secondary corroboration only

review.note: Date, 27 Stat. 1006 and Harrison are right. Predecessor name restored: Pikes Peak Timber Land Reserve (OCR "ikes Peak ^<;mber Land"). It became the Pikes Peak Forest Reserve in 1905 and the Pike NF in 1908.

designationHistory.name: Pike National Forest
designationHistory.indexText: Pikes Peak: Land transferred to Arapaho and Leadville. Land added from Medicine Bow. Name changed to Pike.

sources.name: Establishment and Modification of National Forest Boundaries: A Chronologic Record, 1891–1985 (USDA Forest Service, Lands Staff, 1985), PDF page 29

Presidential Executive Orders, Numbered 1-8030, 1862-1938 (WPA Historical Records Survey, 1944), vol. 1, list entry 888: July 1, 1908, Pike National Forest, Colo., created from portions of the Pikes Peak and Medicine Bow National Forests

Davis, The National Forests of the United States (Encyclopedia of American Forest and Conservation History, App. I, 1983), Forest History Society PDF; compiled partly from an earlier edition of the Forest Service chronologic record, so secondary corroboration only

review.note: Executive Order 888, July 1, 1908, Theodore Roosevelt; Davis treats it as the Pikes Peak to Pike name change, with land changes.
